title: Hard Candy
full_review:
"Hard Candy" (Lionsgate) is a twisted thriller about a crafty 14-year-old honors student, Hayley (Ellen Page), who turns the tables on fashion photographer Jeff (Patrick Wilson), a pervert she met on the Internet. She is convinced he is a pedophile killer -- though his guilt remains ambiguous -- and baits him into a psychological contest of wills planning to exact brutal vigilante justice.

It is troubling that viewers are asked to root for either a sexual deviant looking for young girls or a straight-A sadist, with the child molester coming across as the more sympathetic.

Director David Slade's film starts out as an intriguing cautionary tale, but despite riveting performances quickly descends into exploitative territory, rather than saying anything of substance about its serious subject matter, while its blurred delineation between "victim" and "predator" further muddies its murky morality.

This "Hard Candy" will leave a sour taste in your mouth.

The film contains disturbing scenes of brutality and torture, including an intense castration sequence, a suicide, sexual situations involving a minor, underage drinking, pedophilia theme, and much rough and sexually crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
